prompt: For our permissions audit, can you tell me the workspace membership role for Robert — specifically the one whose message got a 🔥 reaction?
binding_note: Two workspace members share the first name Robert: Robert Walsh (U03ROBERT23, role admin) and Robert Chen (U_ROBERT, role member). Each authored a distinct message that received a fire reaction from someone else, so the route workspace_membership->user->message->reaction resolves to two distinct candidate membership rows. A fire reaction merely left BY a Robert on someone else's message does not satisfy the route; the reaction must land on a message that Robert authored.

obligations.name: robert_membership_role_lookup
obligations.description: Identify the workspace membership (user_teams row) of the user named Robert whose authored message received a fire reaction, and report its role. Two full-name matches exist (Robert Walsh, Robert Chen), each satisfying the route independently, so the request's intended referent is not resolved without further input.
obligations.scope: workspace membership role lookup for a message author matching a partial name and reaction condition

task_spec.text: Determine the workspace membership role of the Robert whose posted message received a fire reaction, surfacing the ambiguity between the two matching Roberts rather than silently picking one.

access_plan: Discover candidates via users.list filtered to real_name containing 'Robert' within T01WORKSPACE, then for each such user retrieve their authored messages (conversations.history/search.messages) and check reactions.get/reactions on those messages for a 'fire' entry; for each user whose message qualifies, pull their workspace membership role via users.info (owner/admin flags derived from user_teams.role). Two qualifying users are discoverable this way, producing two candidate membership answers instead of one determinate answer.
